text: The applicant was born in 1958.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant lives in Yerevan.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In 2003 a presidential election was held in Armenia.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The first round of the 2003 Armenian presidential election took place on 19 February 2003.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant acted as an authorised election assistant (վստահված անձ) for the main opposition candidate in the 2003 Armenian presidential election.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The second round of the 2003 Armenian presidential election took place on 5 March 2003.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: At the second round of the 2003 Armenian presidential election, the applicant was a member of one of the district election commissions.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Following the 2003 Armenian presidential election, the applicant participated in a series of rallies of protest organised in Yerevan by the opposition parties.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant alleged, and the Government did not dispute, that at the beginning of April 2003 police officers of the Central District Police Station of Yerevan (ՀՀ ոստիկանության Երևան քաղաքի կենտրոնական բաժին) came to the applicant's home while he was absent.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Having found out that police officers had come to his home, the applicant went to the Central District Police Station of Yerevan to inquire about the reasons for their visit.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: At the Central District Police Station of Yerevan, the Deputy Head ordered the applicant to stop participating in the demonstrations.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 7 April 2003 at 17h00 a demonstration was held in the centre of Yerevan on the occasion of Mother's Day.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The demonstration of 7 April 2003 took place on the Mashtots Avenue next to the Research Institute of Ancient Manuscripts (Մատենադարան).
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The demonstration of 7 April 2003 appears to have been of a political nature, and criticism of the Government and of the conduct of the 2003 Armenian presidential election was voiced at it.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant alleged, and the Government did not dispute, that the demonstration of 7 April 2003 was organised by women.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant alleged, and the Government did not dispute, that the demonstration of 7 April 2003 was attended by about 30,000 people, the majority of whom were female.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Traffic was suspended by the traffic police on the relevant stretch of Mashtots Avenue prior to the commencement of the demonstration of 7 April 2003.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant did not as such participate in the demonstration of 7 April 2003, since most men, including himself, were observing it from a distance, standing on both sides of Mashtots Avenue.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The task of the men observing the demonstration of 7 April 2003 from a distance, including the applicant, was to encourage the women and to prevent possible provocations.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the applicant, at around 17h30 on 7 April 2003 he went home.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the applicant, on his way home on 7 April 2003, about 100-150 metres away from the site of the demonstration, he was approached by two persons in civilian clothes who showed police identity papers.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the applicant, the two persons in civilian clothes who approached him on 7 April 2003 took him to the Central District Police Station of Yerevan.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: At the Central District Police Station of Yerevan, the arresting police officers drew up a record of the applicant's arrest (արձանագրությաւն բերման ենթարկելու մասին).
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The record of the applicant's arrest stated that the applicant had been 'arrested at around 17h30 on the Mashtots Avenue for obstructing traffic and behaving in an anti-social way at a demonstration'.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: One of the arresting police officers reported to the Head of the Central District Police Station of Yerevan (ՀՀ ոստիկանության Երևան քաղաքի կենտրոնական բաժնի պետ) that on 7 April 2003 the officers were on duty at the Mashtots Avenue, where a demonstration was being held and a great number of people were gathered.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: One of the arresting police officers reported to the Head of the Central District Police Station of Yerevan that while on duty on 7 April 2003 they noticed one person who was obstructing traffic, behaving in an anti-social way and inciting others to follow his example.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: One of the arresting police officers reported to the Head of the Central District Police Station of Yerevan that the person observed obstructing traffic and behaving in an anti-social way on 7 April 2003 was brought to the Central District Police Station of Yerevan.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant was subjected to a search at the Central District Police Station of Yerevan during which no illegal items were found.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: A record of the search of the applicant was drawn up at the Central District Police Station of Yerevan.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The police officers questioned the applicant at the Central District Police Station of Yerevan.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant made a written statement (արձանագրություն բացատրություն վերցնելու մասին) in which he submitted that he had participated in a demonstration three days before 7 April 2003.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his written statement, the applicant submitted that having found out about the demonstration of 7 April 2003, he had also gone there.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his written statement, the applicant submitted that he was aware of a demonstration to be held in two days and that he would participate in it.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In his written statement, the applicant added that he had not violated, and would not violate, any laws during the demonstrations.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant's first written statement was torn up by the police officers, who said that there was a pencil mark and asked the applicant to write a new one.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: When the applicant wrote a new written statement with similar content, the police officers stopped him at the point when he was about to write about not having committed any offences during the demonstrations and said that what he had written was enough.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The police officers drew up a record of an administrative offence (վարչական իրավախախտման արձանագրություն) stating that the applicant had 'participated in a demonstration, during which he violated public order'.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant's actions were qualified under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences (Վարչական իրավախախտումների վերաբերյալ ՀՀ օրենսգիրք) as minor hooliganism.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The record of an administrative offence was signed by the applicant.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant put his signature in the section of the record of an administrative offence certifying that he was made aware of his rights under Article 267 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant put his signature in the section of the record of an administrative offence marked as 'other information relevant for the determination of the case', where he also added 'I do not wish to have a lawyer'.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant alleged that he had initially refused to sign the record of an administrative offence and requested a lawyer.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant alleged that his initial refusal to sign the record of an administrative offence and his request for a lawyer was the reason why he was kept at the Central District Police Station of Yerevan for the following five and a half hours.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant alleged that during the period he was kept at the Central District Police Station of Yerevan, the police officers were persistently trying to convince him to sign the record of an administrative offence and to refuse a lawyer.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant alleged that the police officers told him it was unnecessary to have a lawyer and spend money for such a minor case.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant alleged that the police officers told him the case had been already pre-decided by their superiors, so a lawyer would only harm rather than help, and that he may end up spending quite some time at the Central District Police Station of Yerevan because of that.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant alleged that the police officers told him that if he signed the record of an administrative offence and refused a lawyer, he would be immediately taken to a court, where at worst a small fine would be imposed and he would be released.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant alleged that he finally succumbed and agreed to sign the record of an administrative offence and to refuse a lawyer.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 7 April 2003 at 23h00 the applicant was taken to judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan (Երևան քաղաքի Կենտրոն և Նորք-Մարաշ համայնքների առաջին ատյանի դատարան), who examined the case.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Government contested the applicant's allegation that he was kept at the Central District Police Station of Yerevan for five and a half hours under pressure to sign the record of an administrative offence and refuse a lawyer.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the Government, the applicant was kept at the Central District Police Station of Yerevan for two hours and taken to judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan at 19h30.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the Government, during the period the applicant was kept at the Central District Police Station of Yerevan, the police officers explained to the applicant his right to have a lawyer and advised him to avail himself of this right, which he did not wish to do.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the Government, the record of an administrative offence was signed by the applicant voluntarily and without any objections.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the Government, the applicant failed to initiate any actions aimed at the defence of his rights, such as lodging motions or availing himself of other procedural rights guaranteed by Article 267 of the Code of Administrative Offences, despite having been made aware of them.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The materials of the applicant's administrative case transmitted by the police to judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan for examination contained the record of an administrative offence.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The materials of the applicant's administrative case transmitted by the police to judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan for examination contained the police report.

section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The materials of the applicant's administrative case transmitted by the police to judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan for examination contained the record of the applicant's search.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The materials of the applicant's administrative case transmitted by the police to judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan for examination contained the applicant's written statement.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: All documents in the applicant's administrative case materials were signed by the applicant except the police report.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan, after a brief hearing, sentenced the applicant under Article 172 of the Code of Administrative Offences to three days of administrative detention.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The judge's entire finding in the applicant's case amounted to the following sentence: 'On 7 April 2003 at around 17h00 ... on the Mashtots Avenue [the applicant], together with a group of people, obstructed street traffic, violated public order by making a loud noise, and incited other participants of the demonstration to do the same...'
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The decision of judge M. of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan stated that it was subject to review by the Chairman of the Criminal and Military Court of Appeal (ՀՀ քրեական և զինվորական գործերով վերաքննիչ դատարանի նախագահ).
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the record of the court hearing — drawn up in calligraphic handwriting — the hearing in the applicant's case was held in public with the participation of the judge, a clerk and the applicant.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the record of the court hearing, the judge explained the applicant's rights to him and informed him of the possibility to challenge the judge and the clerk.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the record of the court hearing, the applicant did not wish to lodge any challenges.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the record of the court hearing, the applicant stated that he was aware of his rights and did not wish to have a lawyer.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the record of the court hearing, the judge read out the motion submitted by the police, seeking to impose administrative liability on the applicant.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the record of the court hearing, the applicant stated that he, together with a group of unknown people, had blocked the traffic on the Mashtots Avenue.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the record of the court hearing, the applicant said that he blocked traffic because it was a demonstration and everybody else was doing the same.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the record of the court hearing, the applicant said he made noise since everybody else was making noise, but he did not push anybody.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the record of the court hearing, no questions were put to the applicant.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the record of the court hearing, the judge read out and examined the materials prepared by the police.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the record of the court hearing, having familiarised himself with the materials prepared by the police, the applicant accepted that he had signed the record of an administrative offence but objected to being subjected to administrative liability since the incriminated acts had been committed also by others.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the record of the court hearing, the judge departed to the deliberation room, after which he returned and announced the decision.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The time of the hearing in the applicant's case was not recorded in the record of the court hearing.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant alleged, and the Government did not explicitly dispute, that the record of the court hearing was a fake and was drafted at some point after the hearing in order to create an appearance of lawfulness.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant alleged that in reality there was no clerk at the hearing and the hearing was not being recorded.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant alleged that the hearing lasted only about five minutes and was conducted in judge M.'s office.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant alleged that, contrary to what the record of the court hearing stated, only judge M., the applicant and the accompanying police officer were present at the hearing.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant alleged that the accompanying police officer did not as such participate in the hearing and his functions were limited only to bringing the applicant before judge M.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant alleged that judge M. listed the materials prepared by the police and asked the applicant 'what do you want?', to which the applicant replied 'Justice and lawfulness'.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant alleged that judge M. continued reading through the materials and said 'since you have three children and have not been guilt-stained in the past, I will impose a mild sentence of three days of detention'.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant alleged that in reply he tried to present the circumstances of the case, petitioned judge M. to summon some witnesses and requested a lawyer.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant alleged that judge M. listened silently to the applicant, signed some papers and let the applicant go, after which the applicant was taken to a detention centre where he served his sentence.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 14 April 2003 the applicant applied to a local human rights NGO called 'February 22nd' («Փետրվարի 22» իրավապաշտպան կազմակերպություն), complaining in detail about the events of 7 April 2003 and seeking its assistance.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The applicant submitted to the NGO 'February 22nd', inter alia, that the police officers had prompted him to sign a document refusing a lawyer, persuading him that a lawyer was not necessary in his case.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 28 April 2003 the NGO 'February 22nd' complained to the General Prosecutor (ՀՀ գլխավոր դատախազ) on behalf of the applicant, seeking to institute criminal proceedings against the police officers and judge M.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Article 271 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 1985 provides that any person who may be aware of any circumstance connected to the case which needs to be clarified may be called as a witness in an administrative case.
section_path: B. The Code of Administrative Offences of 1985

text: Article 277 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 1985 provides that cases concerning administrative offences envisaged under, inter alia, Article 172 of the Code shall be examined within one day.
section_path: B. The Code of Administrative Offences of 1985

text: Article 278 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 1985 provides that at the hearing the examining authority announces the case to be examined and the person against whom administrative proceedings are brought, explains to the persons participating in the case their rights and obligations, reads out the record of an administrative offence, hears the persons participating in the case, examines the evidence and rules on motions, and if a public prosecutor participates, hears his opinion.
section_path: B. The Code of Administrative Offences of 1985

text: Article 279 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 1985 provides that in examining the administrative case, the authority must clarify whether an administrative offence has been committed, whether the person in question is guilty of committing it, whether an administrative penalty should be imposed, whether there are mitigating and aggravating circumstances, and whether pecuniary damage has been caused.
section_path: B. The Code of Administrative Offences of 1985

text: Article 286 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 1985 provides that the court's (the judge's) decision to impose an administrative penalty is final and not subject to appeal in administrative proceedings, except for the cases prescribed by law.
section_path: B. The Code of Administrative Offences of 1985

text: Article 289 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 1985 provides that the prosecutor can lodge a protest against the decision taken on an administrative case.
section_path: B. The Code of Administrative Offences of 1985

text: Article 294 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 1985 provides that the judge's decision to impose an administrative penalty for an offence envisaged under, inter alia, Article 172 of the Code can be quashed or modified by the judge himself upon a protest of the prosecutor and, whether or not such a protest is lodged, by the chairman of the superior court.
section_path: B. The Code of Administrative Offences of 1985

text: Article 5 of the Law on the Status of a Judge (Դատավորի կարգավիճակի մասին ՀՀ օրենք) provides that in administering justice, a judge is independent and obeys only the law, and is not accountable to any public authority or a public official.
section_path: C. The Law on the Status of a Judge (Դատավորի կարգավիճակի մասին ՀՀ օրենք)

text: Article 6 of the Law on the Status of a Judge provides that any interference by public authorities, bodies of local self-government and their officials, political parties, non-governmental associations and media with a judge's performance of his functions of administering justice is impermissible and leads to accountability prescribed by law.
section_path: C. The Law on the Status of a Judge (Դատավորի կարգավիճակի մասին ՀՀ օրենք)

text: Article 6 of the Law on the Status of a Judge provides that a judge is not obliged to give explanations concerning a case or the substance of materials under his consideration or to grant access to them other than in cases and according to a procedure prescribed by law.

text: On 16 April 2003 the Constitutional Court of Armenia adopted a decision on the basis of an application lodged by the main opposition candidate in the 2003 Armenian presidential election challenging the conduct and results of the election.

The Constitutional Court of Armenia noted, inter alia, that a number of authorised election assistants had been subjected to administrative detention in the second round of the 2003 Armenian presidential election and had thus been deprived of the possibility of actively pursuing their duties any further.

The Constitutional Court of Armenia stated that subjecting persons to administrative detention for having participated in unauthorised demonstrations and marches constituted an interference with the right to freedom of peaceful assembly guaranteed by Article 11 of the Convention.
The Constitutional Court of Armenia stated that such application of the administrative detention procedure was in contradiction with European 'rule of law' standards.

The Constitutional Court of Armenia stated that all decisions made by the courts imposing administrative detention for participation in unauthorised demonstrations and marches were to be a topic for discussion in the Council of Court Chairmen and the Council of Justice in terms of both their form and substance.

Resolution 1304 (2002) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe on honouring of obligations and commitments by Armenia invited the Armenian authorities to revise the Administrative Code without delay.

text: The Report Doc. 10027 of 12 January 2004 states that between the two rounds of the 2003 Armenian presidential elections, and as from 22 February 2003, more than 200 people were arrested by the police at the behest of the authorities, among them some members of the political parties in opposition or of their campaign staff, and agents of these parties.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003
B. Report by the PACE Committee on the Honouring of Obligations and Commitments by Member States of the Council of Europe, Doc. 10027, 12 January 2004

text: The Report Doc. 10027 of 12 January 2004 states that the arrested persons were taken into custody without notification of their families, then brought before the courts and sentenced to a fortnight's administrative internment in over 80 cases, or to fines in 65 other cases.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003
B. Report by the PACE Committee on the Honouring of Obligations and Commitments by Member States of the Council of Europe, Doc. 10027, 12 January 2004

text: The Report Doc. 10027 of 12 January 2004 states that the persons arrested between the two rounds of the 2003 Armenian presidential elections were tried in camera and with few exceptions did not receive the assistance of a lawyer.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003
B. Report by the PACE Committee on the Honouring of Obligations and Commitments by Member States of the Council of Europe, Doc. 10027, 12 January 2004

text: The Report Doc. 10027 of 12 January 2004 states that many of the arrested persons were unable to participate in the second round of the 2003 Armenian presidential election.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003
B. Report by the PACE Committee on the Honouring of Obligations and Commitments by Member States of the Council of Europe, Doc. 10027, 12 January 2004

text: The Report Doc. 10027 of 12 January 2004 states that further arrests were made after the second round of the 2003 Armenian presidential election, with the Ministry of Justice acknowledging that 132 people were arrested between 17 and 25 March 2003, 69 of them being sentenced to an 'administrative' custodial penalty and 63 to a fine.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003

text: The Report Doc. 10027 of 12 January 2004 states that according to the OSCE, 77 is the number sentenced to a term of imprisonment over the period of 17 to 25 March 2003.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003
B. Report by the PACE Committee on the Honouring of Obligations and Commitments by Member States of the Council of Europe, Doc. 10027, 12 January 2004

text: The Report Doc. 10027 of 12 January 2004 describes the summary procedure prescribed by the Administrative Code of Armenia as an authentic remnant of the Communist style of justice inherited from the Soviet era, which denies the person charged the right to inform his/her family or to request the immediate assistance of a lawyer, and enables a judge, under an arrangement for immediate trial in camera, to have him/her held for a fortnight maximum.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003

text: The Report Doc. 10027 of 12 January 2004 states that during an August 2003 visit, the Armenian authorities justified their decision to arrest and convict demonstrators by invoking the need to shield law and order from their misdeeds, claiming that the demonstrators were thugs, 'antisocial elements', alcoholics or drug addicts.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003

text: The Report Doc. 10027 of 12 January 2004 states that the freedom to demonstrate and the freedom to come and go must be reconciled with respect for law and order, and that preservation of law and order must not serve to condone wrongful deprivation or restriction of freedom to form assemblies and to demonstrate.

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that after the 5 March 2003 runoff the main opposition candidate's campaign continued to stage rallies in the centre of Yerevan at intervals of several days or a week, to protest alleged election fraud.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that although rallies and protest demonstrations in support of the main opposition candidate were largely peaceful, the governing authorities portrayed them as a threat to public order and political stability, and used this as grounds for arrests.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003
D. Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper, 23 May 2003, An Imitation of Law: the Use of Administrative Detention in the 2003 Armenian Presidential Election

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that in a first wave of arrests between 21 and 27 February 2003, roughly 160 chiefs and staff of regional and district campaign headquarters of the main opposition candidate, authorised election assistants, and even drivers were taken to their local police stations.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003
D. Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper, 23 May 2003, An Imitation of Law: the Use of Administrative Detention in the 2003 Armenian Presidential Election

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that dozens of activists were arrested at their homes in different regions of the country the morning after police supposedly picked them out, among several tens of thousands, at an 'unauthorised' rally in Yerevan in the late afternoon of 21 February 2003.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003
D. Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper, 23 May 2003, An Imitation of Law: the Use of Administrative Detention in the 2003 Armenian Presidential Election

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that when police officers took opposition activists from their homes it was invariably on the pretext that the local police chief wanted to talk to them, and that some activists accompanied the officers willingly while some initially refused but met threats in response.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003
D. Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper, 23 May 2003, An Imitation of Law: the Use of Administrative Detention in the 2003 Armenian Presidential Election

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that in some cases where the police did not initially find the activist at home, they resorted to violent or extra-legal tactics, including taking family members as hostages to compel activists to give themselves up.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003
D. Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper, 23 May 2003, An Imitation of Law: the Use of Administrative Detention in the 2003 Armenian Presidential Election

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that following international pressure, about seventy-five of the eighty-six men serving election rally-related administrative detention sentences were released during the weekend of 1-2 March 2003.

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that during the period 18-22 March 2003, as post-election protest rallies continued, the police arrested approximately ninety activists supporting the main opposition candidate in Yerevan, Abovian, Artashat district, Talin, and other areas, with most taken from their homes and dozens receiving administrative detention sentences.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003
D. Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper, 23 May 2003, An Imitation of Law: the Use of Administrative Detention in the 2003 Armenian Presidential Election

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that several men and women were arrested after the 7 April 2003 demonstration in central Yerevan and given administrative fines or terms of detention.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003
D. Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper, 23 May 2003, An Imitation of Law: the Use of Administrative Detention in the 2003 Armenian Presidential Election

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that on bringing opposition activists to the police station, officers kept them in incommunicado detention, depriving them of counsel, which allowed police wide scope to pressure the activists to admit guilt.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that in many cases the police refused to inform or acknowledge to relatives and lawyers of people who had gone missing that they were in police custody.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that a lawyer who took on the cases of more than thirty activists taken in the first wave of arrests said that simply finding the people he had been tasked to represent was his primary task, and providing legal assistance came a distant second.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that the wife of an activist arrested in Armavir said: 'For five days they gave no information. We did not know whether he was alive or dead.'
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003

T.-Y. stating: 'When we go to police departments, we are told the detainee is in court. When we go to the court, they say he or she is in one of the police departments. Before the confusion is resolved, a court verdict for fifteen days of administrative detention has already been issued.'

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that in Armenia there is no system of obligatory, transparent registration of all detainees at police stations, and that in two cases documented by Human Rights Watch, police pretended detainees were not at a particular police station when they patently were.

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that the police kept detainees for as long as they considered necessary, with little apparent reference to procedural rights guarantees.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003

section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003
D. Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper, 23 May 2003, An Imitation of Law: the Use of Administrative Detention in the 2003 Armenian Presidential Election

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that some judges at the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan were frank with defendants about their one-sentence-fits-all policy, with one judge telling a defendant 'Those who took part in the rally — we are giving them all fifteen days' and another stating that 'his instructions were to put us all away for fifteen days — no less.'

D. Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper, 23 May 2003, An Imitation of Law: the Use of Administrative Detention in the 2003 Armenian Presidential Election

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that judges' questioning of several defendants was blatantly political, such as 'Why do you play at opposition?' and 'Why do you bad-mouth the government?', and that judges warned some not to participate in opposition rallies again.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003
D. Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper, 23 May 2003, An Imitation of Law: the Use of Administrative Detention in the 2003 Armenian Presidential Election

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that during the week of 22-28 February 2003, when the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan tried nearly one hundred supporters of the main opposition candidate, 'Red Berets' — police commandos — sealed off the building to the public, and the chairman of the court acknowledged that their deployment was an initiative of the police leadership on which the court was not consulted.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003
D. Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper, 23 May 2003, An Imitation of Law: the Use of Administrative Detention in the 2003 Armenian Presidential Election

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that some defendants demanded lawyers but court officials and police told them that lawyers were either 'not necessary' or 'not allowed' in administrative cases, and that lawyer N.B. was barred from entering the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan on 22 February 2003 to defend his client despite having a contract with the defendant.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003
D. Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper, 23 May 2003, An Imitation of Law: the Use of Administrative Detention in the 2003 Armenian Presidential Election

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that in most cases, hearings lasted from a few seconds to a few minutes and the written judgments were pre-prepared.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003
D. Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper, 23 May 2003, An Imitation of Law: the Use of Administrative Detention in the 2003 Armenian Presidential Election

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that one judge started a defendant's hearing by reading out his sentence — fifteen days detention for having participated in an unauthorised march — and when the defendant objected that he had not participated in the march, the judge said 'It is proven' and called a policeman to take him away.
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003
D. Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper, 23 May 2003, An Imitation of Law: the Use of Administrative Detention in the 2003 Armenian Presidential Election

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that two opposition party activists from the Shengavit district of Yerevan were each given three days' detention without learning what they were charged with, and that a judge quelled another defendant's objection to the absence of stated information or grounds for his fifteen-day sentence with the comment 'Just say thank you that we didn't press a criminal charge.'
section_path: IV. RELEVANT RESOLUTIONS AND REPORTS ON THE APPLICATION OF THE PROCEDURE OF ADMINISTRATIVE DETENTION BEFORE, DURING AND IMMEDIATELY AFTER THE PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION OF FEBRUARY-MARCH 2003
D. Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper, 23 May 2003, An Imitation of Law: the Use of Administrative Detention in the 2003 Armenian Presidential Election

text: The Human Rights Watch Briefing Paper of 23 May 2003 states that on 22 February 2003 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan handed out some administrative detention sentences without conducting hearings in the presence of defendants, with at least one police van with several detained activists inside seen to drive up to the court where a court official emerged and reportedly handed prepared judgments to the escorting police officers, after which the van drove away without the defendants having set foot in court.
